title: The Polyglot Pick-Up Line Fail (Wrong Formality Level)
style: smooth lo-fi hip hop, J-pop trap fusion, 90 BPM, charming but clumsy male lead, soft female harmonies, vinyl crackle, mellow piano keys, boom bap drums, koto sample, shamisen pluck, EN/ES/JP codeswitch, romantic-comedic, hooky chorus, late night radio vibe
lyrics:
[Intro — lo-fi vinyl crackle, soft jazz piano]
Round one… smooth confidence engaged
[record scratch]
Round two… formality misfire
[record scratch]
Round three… we don't talk about round three

[Verse 1 — EN, smooth lo-fi flow]
Hey girl, you must be a dictionary
'cause you add meaning to my life every day
She smiled, I smiled, the moment was airy
Then I said "let's hang out" — and threw it away

[Verse 2 — ES, charming but clumsy]
Eres como un diccionario, mi alma
Porque le das sentido a mi vida entera
She laughed, I leaned, ordered horchata calma
Then I called her "tú" — should've been "usted," era

[Verse 3 — JP, J-pop trap fusion]
Anata wa jisho mitai, kawaii desu ne
Watashi no seikatsu ni imi o ataeru yo
She bowed, I bowed, the rhythm felt okay
Then I dropped the keigo — used "omae" — dame yo!

[Pre-Chorus — multi-lingual confessional]
Three languages, three shots, three formality fails
The vocab was perfect, the register derailed
"Tú" when I needed "usted," "omae" when I needed "anata"
The dictionary was fine — the SOCIAL LAYER was the saga

[Chorus — three voices stacked, smooth into chaotic]
But then I said "I love you" in the wrong formality level
Now she's bowing, I'm sweating, the dictionary's dead!
Te amo, te quiero — same words, different planet
Aishiteru is too strong — I should've said "suki da" yet!

[Verse 4 — what went wrong, slow breakdown]
Spanish has tú and usted and vos
Japanese has casual, polite, humble, honored, AND boss
English just has "you" — we think we have it easy
But we miss the layer that the others find breezy

[Bridge — spoken, regretful]
She texted back: "你太直接了"
That's Chinese, not even one of the three I tried
The dictionary added a fourth language to the night
The polyglot pick-up line officially died

[Final Chorus]
But then I said "I love you" in the wrong formality level
Now she's bowing, I'm sweating, the dictionary's dead!
Te amo, te quiero — same words, different planet
Aishiteru is too strong — I should've said "suki da" yet!

[Outro — whispered, vinyl fade]
Sumimasen. Lo siento. My bad.
